name: Youth Brigade
label: Dischord
lede: Nathan Strejcek and Danny Ingram, two Wilson High friends from bands that had just ended, start Youth Brigade in late 1980 and are finished by December 1981. They leave eleven songs on Dischord, and D.C. has to wait thirty years for more.

eras.title: Two bands end, one starts
eras.text: By late 1980 the first wave of D.C. kid bands had burned through. The Teen Idles and the Untouchables were done, and Strejcek, who had sung for the first and Ingram, who had drummed for the second, weren't.

years.h: Nathan Strejcek and Danny Ingram start over as Youth Brigade
years.p: With [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and the [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]] both split, singer [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] and drummer [[Danny Ingram|41959411-d1b4-4954-af09-087ac72f69ab]] form a new band. Dischord adds a note: not the Youth Brigade from Los Angeles.
years.xp:
Strejcek had briefly run Dischord after the Teen Idles ended. According to Wikipedia, Jeff Nelson and Ian MacKaye were disappointed by how little he put into it and took the label back.

Ingram had only started drumming when the Untouchables lost their drummer and he volunteered, never having played before.

years.h: After a guitarist and a bassist named Greg, the lineup sticks
years.p: [[John Falls|44fd383a-ff3f-4028-8cc9-b01b71f5b2dc]] plays guitar for a while, and a bassist remembered only as Greg passes through. Then [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]], Ingram's old Untouchables bandmate, takes bass and Tom Clinton takes guitar.

eras.title: Nine months, one van
eras.text: Youth Brigade's whole life fits inside 1981: a first show in March, a last one in December. In between they opened for Black Flag, lost a tour when Tom Clinton's mother wanted her van back, and made the Possible EP, Dischord No. 6.

years.h: Food for Thought hosts the first Youth Brigade show
years.p: The Dupont Circle restaurant doubled as a D.C. punk room. Dischord dates the debut March 1981.

years.cap: Youth Brigade at the 9:30 Club, Washington, D.C., around 1981
years.h: Youth Brigade open for Black Flag on its first East Coast trip
years.p: The bill at the 9:30 club is Black Flag, [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and Youth Brigade, a few weeks into the band's life.
years.xp:
Dischord says Youth Brigade and Minor Threat opened for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] at the 9:30 club. Wikipedia goes further and credits Youth Brigade with playing the first Black Flag show on the East Coast, shortly after its March debut.

Neither source gives an exact date beyond 1981.

years.h: Tom Clinton's mother wants her van back
years.p: Youth Brigade are on the road with Minor Threat when, according to Wikipedia, Clinton's mother, who owns the van, demands it. The tour ends early.

years.h: Nine months after the first show, the last one
years.p: Dischord's dates for Youth Brigade end in December 1981, the same month as the Possible EP.

years.h: A joke in a Dischord ad becomes Possible, Dischord No. 6
years.p: Michael Bishop of [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]], on Barbed Wire. Eight songs in under ten minutes; the title comes from one of the label's first ads, which listed a "Possible EP" among future releases.
years.xp:
Maximum Rocknroll heard a chunkier, slightly slower thrash than Minor Threat. The closing track, No Song II, lasts one second.

Bishop pointed to the sound of Barbed Wire, drowning in delay and reverb, as what made it crucial.

eras.title: Filed under Dischord history
eras.text: Youth Brigade was gone before most of D.C. heard it. Dischord kept the songs in circulation, first on the sampler Flex Your Head, then on Four Old 7"s on a 12", which saved the early singles from collector prices.

years.h: Flex Your Head gives Youth Brigade three more songs
years.p: Moral Majority, Waste of Time and Last Word land on Dischord's scene sampler. With the EP, that makes 11 Youth Brigade songs released while the band lasted.

years.h: Queiroz heads to Rain, Ingram to Dot Dash, Strejcek leaves the scene
years.p: Queiroz goes on to [[Rain|4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983]] and [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]]; Ingram to [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], [[Dot Dash|fce03e2d-8138-4418-b29e-499f61c6800e]] and, per Wikipedia, [[Swervedriver|fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0]].
years.xp: Queiroz also played in Double-O and Second Wind, and Ingram in Emmapeel.

years.h: Four Old 7"s on a 12" keeps Possible in print
years.p: Dischord gathers the EP with early singles by [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]], [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] and [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]], long after the originals vanished.

eras.title: Back for a documentary
eras.text: Thirty years on, the Salad Days documentary about the D.C. scene needed money, and Strejcek, Ingram and Bert Queiroz came back to help. Dischord then released the summer 1981 session as Complete First Demo.

years.cap: Youth Brigade at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C., December 29, 2012
years.h: Salad Days needs money, so Youth Brigade play again
years.p: Strejcek, Ingram and Queiroz reunite at the Black Cat for a benefit for the documentary. On guitar is [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]], ex-[[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]].

years.cap: Youth Brigade at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C., December 29, 2012
years.h: Back at the 9:30 Club for the Punk-Funk Throwdown
years.p: The reunited band, with Hansgen on guitar, plays a second reunion date in February.
Out of the scene for decades, the former Youth Brigade singer starts a new band. According to Wikipedia, they release Irradiate in 2023.

years.src: Dischord: Complete First Demo · Wikipedia: Youth Brigade
years.h: Thirty-four years on, the first session finally gets a proper release
years.p: Youth Brigade recorded eight tracks at Inner Ear in summer 1981 with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] and [[Skip Groff|8c4d8d50-a6a7-4fa6-9524-6e9c595816c1]]. Many had never been officially released before Dischord put out Complete First Demo.
years.xp:
Dischord pressed it as a 7" on yellow vinyl, and its news post sums up the band: first show in March 1981, a run of "a little over a year."

Wikipedia cites critic Alexander Lalama calling it a "gem" and a "historical document."
play: It's About Time That We Had a Change

sources.title: Dischord: Complete First Demo out November 23
